newsitem.title: USA: USDA to hold civil rights "listening sessions".
newsitem.headline: USDA to hold civil rights "listening sessions".

text.p: The Agriculture Department Tuesday said it will hold a series of "listening sessions" across the country in January on alleged discrimination in its farmer loan programs with top officials attending.

"We have a real opportunity to make positive change in the area of civil rights enforcement at USDA and to ensure that both our employees and customers are treated fairly and with diginity," Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said in a statement. "I am committed to bringing about that change."
Glickman or Deputy Secretary Richard Rominger will be at each "listening session", the department said.

Black farmers have long contended that they endure discrimination in USDA lending programs and that racism was the basis for loan rejections and foreclosures. A group of black producers rallied in front of the White House earlier this month and met with Glickman.
USDA has set up a civil rights action team to probe the complaints and suspended government farm foreclosures pending review, among other actions.

Sessions are scheduled in Albany, Ga. on Jan. 6; New Orleans and Memphis on Jan. 7; Halifax, N.C. on Jan. 8; Tulsa on Jan. 10; Brownsville, Texas on Jan. 11; Window Rock, Ariz on Jan. 13; Salinas, Calif. on Jan 16; Sacramento on Jan. 17; Rapid City, S.D. on Jan. 18, Washington, D.C. on Jan. 22 and Belzoni, Miss. on Jan. 24.
The New Orleans and Sacramento sessions are in-house for department employees only.
